column5: Preconditions

column1: Verify the whole-work-order Add dialog opens from the WO toolbar more (⋯) menu at Whole Work Order scope
column5:
1. You are logged in as a role that has Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open (not Invoiced, not Paid) work order exists; you are viewing it and are NOT in history mode.
3. You are on the work order's Lines tab.
column6:
1. Click the ⋯ (More actions) menu at the top-right of the work order toolbar.
2. Click the menu item 'Add Fee/Discount'.
3. Observe the dialog title and any subtitle.
column7:
1. A dialog opens with the title 'Add new fee/discount' and the work order number (e.g. 'S2-13274') shown as the context subtitle.
2. There is NO 'Applying to:' subtitle, because Whole Work Order scope has none.
3. The scope is Whole Work Order and cannot be changed from inside the dialog (there is no scope dropdown).

column1: Verify adding a whole-WO Flat Amount fee saves and shows the success toast
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with subtotal exactly $10,715.39 (or any known subtotal) is open on the Lines tab.
column6:
1. Open the ⋯ menu and click 'Add Work Order Fee / Discount'.
2. In the 'Name' field type 'ZZAUTOTEST Handling Fee'.
3. In the 'Type' dropdown select 'Fee'.
4. In the 'Calculation type' dropdown select 'Flat amount'.
5. In the 'Amount' field enter 100 (shown with a $ prefix).
6. Leave 'Max cap' empty.
7. Click the confirm button ('Add Fee' per spec / 'Add' in the design mockup).
column7:
1. The Amount field shows a '$' prefix once 'Flat amount' is chosen (design updateCalcUI()).
2. The confirm button becomes enabled (Name, Type, Calc type, Amount>0 all set).
3. On save the dialog closes and a success toast reads 'Fee added' (§7), fading on its own.
4. The adjustment 'ZZAUTOTEST Handling Fee' now appears in the sidebar 'Work Order Fee / Discount' card with a '+$100.00' rate badge and a grey resolved amount of +$100.00.
5. The work order subtotal/total reflect +$100.00 (tax recalculated on save).

column1: Verify the live preview computes and displays a whole-WO percentage discount (8% of $10,715.39 → −$857.23)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with Work Order Total = $10,715.39 is open.
column6:
1. Open 'Add Work Order Fee / Discount' from the ⋯ menu.
2. Set Type = 'Discount'.
3. Set Calculation type = 'Percentage'.
4. In the Amount field enter 8 (shown with a '%' suffix).
5. Read the live preview block.
column7:
1. Preview row 'Work Order Total' shows $10,715.39.
2. Preview row label flips to 'Discount' and shows −$857.23 (8% × 10,715.39 = 857.2312, rounded to nearest cent = 857.23; §5-R3).
3. Preview row 'New Work Order Total' shows $9,858.16.
4. The bottom of the preview reads 'Tax is recalculated on save.' (S2-R35).
5. The discount amount is signed and colored (the exact color differs between spec and design).

column1: Verify 'Apply from template' auto-fills the dialog fields with the template's values
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order is open; the location's template library contains 'Fleet Standard Discount (−10%)'.
column6:
1. Open 'Add Work Order Fee / Discount'.
2. Open the 'Apply from template (optional)' dropdown.
3. Select 'Fleet Standard Discount (−10%)'.
4. Observe the Name, Type, Calculation type, and Amount fields.
column7:
1. Name is filled with 'Fleet Standard Discount'.
2. Type is set to 'Discount'.
3. Calculation type is set to 'Percentage'.
4. Amount is filled with 10 (with a '%' suffix).
5. Only method, amount, taxable, and Max Amount are copied — the scope stays Whole Work Order (the template never carries a scope; S2-R13).
6. The confirm button is enabled.

column1: Verify the Add button is disabled until Name, Type, Calculation type and Amount>0 are all set
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order is open with the Add dialog freshly opened (all fields blank).
column6:
1. Observe the Add button state with all fields blank.
2. Type a Name only; observe the Add button.
3. Add Type = 'Fee'; observe.
4. Add Calculation type = 'Flat amount'; observe.
5. Enter Amount = 0; observe.
6. Change Amount to 25; observe.
column7:
1. With all fields blank, the Add button is disabled.
2. With only Name filled, Add stays disabled.
3. With Name + Type, Add stays disabled.
4. With Name + Type + Calc type but no amount, Add stays disabled.
5. With Amount = 0, Add stays disabled (amount must be > 0).
6. With Amount = 25 and all other required fields set, Add becomes enabled. Max cap is NOT required.

column1: Verify Max Amount (Max cap) caps a percentage adjustment (20% fee on $100 → +$15 with Max $15)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order whose relevant base for the fee is exactly $100.00 is open.
column6:
1. Open the Add dialog for the whole WO.
2. Set Type = 'Fee', Calculation type = 'Percentage', Amount = 20.
3. Enter Max cap / 'Max Amount (Optional)' = 15.
4. Read the preview, then Save.
column7:
1. The raw computed fee is $20.00 (20% × $100).
2. Because Max Amount is $15.00 and $20.00 > $15.00, the resolved fee is lowered to +$15.00 (§5-R6).
3. The saved adjustment resolves to +$15.00.

column1: Verify the add confirm button label follows the Type (Add Fee vs Add Discount)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. The whole-WO Add dialog is open.
column6:
1. Set Type = 'Fee'; read the confirm button label.
2. Change Type = 'Discount'; read the confirm button label again.
column7:
1. With Type = 'Fee' the confirm button reads 'Add Fee'.
2. With Type = 'Discount' the confirm button reads 'Add Discount' — the label changes live with the Type field (S2-R27).

column1: Verify an empty Name blocks saving a whole-WO adjustment
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. The whole-WO Add dialog is open.
column6:
1. Leave Name blank.
2. Set Type = 'Fee', Calculation type = 'Flat amount', Amount = 10.
3. Attempt to save.
column7:
1. Save is blocked. Per spec S2-N1 an inline error is shown on Name.
2. In the design mockup the effect is that the Add button stays disabled while Name is empty (no inline error rendered).

column1: Verify an empty or zero Amount blocks saving a whole-WO adjustment
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. The whole-WO Add dialog is open with Name, Type='Fee', Calc type='Flat amount' set.
column6:
1. Leave Amount empty; attempt to save.
2. Enter Amount = 0; attempt to save.
column7:
1. With Amount empty, save is blocked (spec S2-N2 inline error; design keeps Add disabled).
2. With Amount = 0, save is blocked because values must be > 0 (Flat smallest $0.01, percentage smallest 0.01%; §5-R1).

column1: Verify a percentage discount over 100% is rejected while a percentage fee has no upper limit
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. The whole-WO Add dialog is open.
column6:
1. Set Type = 'Discount', Calculation type = 'Percentage', Amount = 150; attempt to save.
2. Change Type = 'Fee', keep Percentage, Amount = 150; attempt to save.
column7:
1. A 150% discount is invalid and is rejected (percentage discounts must be ≤ 100%; §5-R2).
2. A 150% fee is accepted (percentage fees have no upper limit; §5-R2).

column1: Verify whole-WO percentage methods resolve against the correct base (% of Subtotal example)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with Net Labor total $200.00, Net Parts total $100.00, Shop Supplies $0.00 (so Subtotal = $300.00), no other adjustments.
column6:
1. Open 'Add Work Order Fee / Discount'.
2. Set Type = 'Fee', Calculation type = '% of Subtotal', Amount = 10.
3. Read the preview, then Save.
column7:
1. The dialog offers whole-WO methods Flat Amount, % of Labor Total, % of Parts Total, % of Subtotal (§5-R10).
2. '% of Subtotal' resolves against Net Labor + Net Parts + Shop Supplies = $300.00.
3. 10% of $300.00 = +$30.00; the saved adjustment resolves to +$30.00.
4. A '% of Grand Total' option is NOT offered (Processing-Fee-only).

column1: Verify 'Add Fee / Discount' is hidden and rejected on an Invoiced or Paid work order
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. A work order in Invoiced (or Paid) status is open.
column6:
1. Open the WO toolbar ⋯ menu and look for 'Add Work Order Fee / Discount'.
2. Hover a labor line and a part row and look for their 'Add fee / discount' items.
column7:
1. 'Add Work Order Fee / Discount' is not shown in the toolbar ⋯ menu (S1-N1).
2. The labor-line and part-row 'Add fee / discount' starting places are not shown either.
3. If the add is triggered by any other route the system rejects it (S3-R1b).

column1: Verify whole-WO starting places are hidden without Work Orders: Create & Edit
column5:
1. Logged in as a role that HAS See Financial Data but does NOT have Work Orders: Create & Edit.
2. An open work order is open.
column6: 1. Open the WO toolbar ⋯ menu and look for 'Add Work Order Fee / Discount'.
column7:
1. 'Add Work Order Fee / Discount' is not shown (S1-N2, S13-N2).
2. Existing whole-WO adjustment dollar amounts are still visible (See Financial Data is ON) but have no Edit/Delete controls.

column1: Verify the live preview shows the empty-amount prompt before an amount is entered
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. The whole-WO Add dialog is freshly open.
column6:
1. Set Type and Calculation type but leave Amount blank.
2. Read the preview block.
column7:
1. Per spec S2-R41 the preview reads 'Enter an amount to see the impact.'
2. In the design mockup the 'Fee / Discount' preview value starts as an em dash '—' until Type is chosen.

column1: Verify the preview adjustment row is signed and colored (fee vs discount)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. The whole-WO Add dialog is open.
column6:
1. Set Type = 'Fee', Calculation type = 'Flat amount', Amount = 50; read the preview color/sign.
2. Change Type = 'Discount'; read the preview color/sign again.
column7:
1. Per spec S2-R33 the fee amount shows in green with a '+' sign and the discount amount shows in red with a '−' sign; this is the only place green/red are used (S12-R2).
2. Preview is signed (+ for fee, − for discount) and updates live.

column1: Verify a labor line's 3-dot menu opens the Add dialog locked to that Labor Line scope
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line, e.g. Line 1 'Service - Perform LOF and inspection', is open on the Lines tab.
column6:
1. Hover the labor line row (or its Labor sub-row) to reveal the ⋯ (More actions) button.
2. Click the ⋯ button and click 'Add fee / discount'.
3. Read the dialog title and subtitle.
column7:
1. The dialog opens locked to Labor Line scope for that specific line.
2. A grey subtitle reads 'Applying to: {line name}' (e.g. 'Applying to: Service - Perform LOF and inspection'); it does NOT include a 'Line {N} Labor —' prefix.
3. Scope/target cannot be changed inside the dialog.

column1: Verify a labor-line % of Labor Total fee resolves against the line's gross labor price (10% of $150.00 → +$15.00)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line whose gross labor price is exactly $150.00, no existing adjustments on that line.
column6:
1. Open the labor line's ⋯ menu and click 'Add fee / discount'.
2. Confirm the default Calculation type is '% of Labor Total' (labor line default per S2-R22).
3. Set Type = 'Fee', Amount = 10.
4. Read the preview, then Save.
column7:
1. The available methods are only Flat Amount and % of Labor Total (§5-R10).
2. The base is the target labor line price (gross) = $150.00 (§5-R4).
3. 10% × $150.00 = +$15.00; the resolved amount is +$15.00 (§5-R3).
4. The preview labels read 'Line labor total → New line labor total' (S2-R36a).

column1: Verify each labor line row exposes its own 3-dot menu on hover
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with two or more labor lines is open on the Lines tab.
column6:
1. Hover over the first labor line row.
2. Hover over the second labor line row.
column7:
1. Each labor line row reveals its own ⋯ (More actions) button on hover (S1-R2).
2. Each menu includes an 'Add fee / discount' item scoped to that specific line.

column1: Verify a labor-line Flat Amount resolves to the exact amount with no quantity multiplier
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line (any quantity/hours) is open.
column6:
1. Open the labor line's ⋯ menu and click 'Add fee / discount'.
2. Set Type = 'Fee', Calculation type = 'Flat amount', Amount = 50.
3. Save.
column7:
1. The resolved amount is exactly +$50.00 regardless of hours/quantity (Labor Line Flat Amount has no quantity part; §5-R14).
2. Max Amount is not available for a Flat Amount method (§5-R6).

column1: Verify a labor-line adjustment resolves to $0.00 when its line is not billable (declined)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line that carries a 10% fee adjustment resolving to a non-zero amount.
column6:
1. Mark / set the labor line to Declined (not billable).
2. Observe the labor-line adjustment's resolved amount.
3. Re-authorize / make the line billable again.
4. Observe the resolved amount again.
column7:
1. While the line is declined/not billable, the adjustment resolves to $0.00 but still shows (§5-R12).
2. Once the line becomes billable/authorized, the adjustment resolves to its non-zero amount again.

column1: Verify deleting a labor line removes any adjustment pointing to it
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line that carries at least one fee/discount adjustment.
column6:
1. Delete the labor line (via its ⋯ / delete action).
2. Check the sidebar card, Financial Info 'Fees & Discounts (N)' count, and Stats breakdown.
column7:
1. The labor line is removed.
2. Any adjustment that pointed to that line is also removed (S3-R2).
3. The Financial Info 'Fees & Discounts (N)' count and the Stats/Financial totals drop by the removed adjustment(s).

column1: Verify labor-line 'Add fee / discount' is hidden without Work Order Lines: Create & Edit
column5:
1. Logged in as a role with See Financial Data but WITHOUT Work Order Lines: Create & Edit.
2. An open work order with a labor line is open.
column6:
1. Hover the labor line and open its ⋯ menu.
2. Look for 'Add fee / discount' and Edit/Delete on any existing line adjustment.
column7:
1. 'Add fee / discount' is not shown for the labor line (S13-N2).
2. Existing line adjustment amounts are still visible (SFD on) but have no Edit/Delete controls.

column1: Verify a part's menu opens the Add dialog locked to that Part Line scope
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part, e.g. '(LF3620) Engine Oil Filter', is open on the Lines or Parts tab.
column6:
1. Hover the part row to reveal its ⋯ menu.
2. Click 'Add fee / discount'.
3. Read the dialog subtitle.
column7:
1. The dialog opens locked to Part Line scope for that part (S1-R5).
2. The grey subtitle reads 'Applying to: Line {N} Part — (LF3620) Engine Oil Filter' (S2-R11), with the part number omitted when the part has none.
3. The available Calculation methods are Flat Amount and % of Parts Total only (§5-R10).

column1: Verify a part-line Flat Amount is charged PER ITEM (amount × quantity): $5.00 × qty 3 → −$15.00
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part of quantity 3.
column6:
1. Open the part's ⋯ menu and click 'Add fee / discount'.
2. Set Type = 'Discount', Calculation type = 'Flat amount', Amount = 5.
3. Save.
4. Read the resolved amount on the inline part row.
column7:
1. The resolved discount is −$15.00 ($5.00 per item × quantity 3; §5-R14).
2. The inline part row shows the discount name with a −$5.00 flat rate badge and a resolved amount of −$15.00.
3. The Add modal Amount label indicates a per-item rate for a Part Line Flat Amount (S2-R23).

column1: Verify a fee/discount can be added to a requested (not-yet-received) part and shows before pick
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a requested (pending / not yet picked) part of quantity 2 at sell price $20.00 each.
column6:
1. Open the requested part's ⋯ menu and click 'Add fee / discount'.
2. Set Type = 'Discount', Calculation type = '% of Parts Total', Amount = 10.
3. Save.
4. Observe the adjustment on the requested part before it is picked/received.
column7:
1. The part's menu offered 'Add fee / discount' for the requested part (S1-R4).
2. The adjustment shows on the requested part before it is picked (§5-R13).
3. It resolves against quantity × sell price = 2 × $20.00 = $40.00 → 10% = −$4.00.

column1: Verify a part-line % of Parts Total resolves against quantity × sell price (gross)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part of quantity 3 at sell price $20.00 each (gross part total $60.00).
column6:
1. Open the part's ⋯ menu and click 'Add fee / discount'.
2. Set Type = 'Discount', Calculation type = '% of Parts Total', Amount = 10.
3. Read the preview, then Save.
column7:
1. The base is quantity × sell price (gross) = 3 × $20.00 = $60.00 (§5-R4).
2. 10% × $60.00 = −$6.00; the resolved amount is −$6.00 (§5-R3).
3. The preview shows a 'Part cost' row (unit cost × quantity) and labels 'Part total → New part total' (S2-R40, S2-R36b).

column1: Verify a part-line adjustment stays attached when the part changes from requested to received
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a requested part that already carries a % of Parts Total discount.
column6:
1. Pick / receive the requested part so it becomes a received part.
2. Observe the adjustment on the now-received part.
column7:
1. The adjustment stays attached to the part after requested → received (§5-R13).
2. It continues to resolve against quantity × sell price.
3. A received part cannot be re-pointed back to a request (§5-R13).

column1: Verify a part-line adjustment resolves to $0.00 when the part is declined or returned with no quantity left
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part carrying a discount that resolves to a non-zero amount.
column6:
1. Decline the part (or return it so no quantity is left).
2. Observe the adjustment's resolved amount.
3. Re-authorize the part (make it billable again).
4. Observe the resolved amount again.
column7:
1. While the part is not billable, the adjustment resolves to $0.00 but stays visible (§5-R12).
2. When the part becomes billable (authorized, not declined, quantity left) it resolves to its non-zero amount again.

column1: Verify deleting a part removes any adjustment pointing to it
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part that carries at least one adjustment.
column6:
1. Delete the part from the work order.
2. Check the Financial Info 'Fees & Discounts (N)' count and the Stats breakdown.
column7:
1. The part is removed.
2. Any adjustment pointing to that part is also removed (S3-R2).
3. The 'Fees & Discounts (N)' count and totals decrease accordingly.

column1: Verify per-item Flat Amount edge: quantity 1 resolves to the base amount (−$5.00)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part of quantity 1.
column6:
1. Open the part's ⋯ menu and add a Flat Amount discount of $5.00.
2. Save and read the resolved amount.
3. Change the part quantity from 1 to 4 and re-check the resolved amount.
column7:
1. At quantity 1 the resolved discount is −$5.00 ($5.00 × 1; §5-R14).
2. After changing the quantity to 4 the adjustment re-resolves to −$20.00 ($5.00 × 4).

column1: Verify a labor-line adjustment shows inline under its line with ↳ arrow, name, signed rate badge and grey amount
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where Line 1 labor carries a 'Line discount' of −5% resolving to −$26.08.
column6:
1. Go to the Lines tab and locate Line 1.
2. Read the inline adjustment row shown under the line title.
column7:
1. The adjustment shows indented under the labor line with a '↳' arrow (S3-R12, S12-R3).
2. It shows the name 'Line discount' and a signed rate badge '−5%' (percentage; extra zeros removed, S3-R6).
3. The resolved dollar amount −$26.08 shows in the cost/Total column in plain grey, signed (S3-R14, S12-R1).

column1: Verify a part-line adjustment shows inline under its part with ↳ arrow, name, signed rate badge and grey amount
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where part '(LF3620) Engine Oil Filter' carries a 'Parts Handling Fee' of +$3.75.
column6:
1. Go to the Lines tab and locate the LF3620 part row.
2. Read the inline adjustment row under the part.
column7:
1. The adjustment shows indented under the part with a '↳' arrow (S3-R13).
2. It shows the name 'Parts Handling Fee' with a signed rate badge (e.g. '+$3.75' Flat or '+2%' percentage).
3. The resolved amount +$3.75 shows in the Total column in plain grey, signed (S3-R14).

column1: Verify a line/part with 2+ adjustments shows only the first plus a 'Show N more' toggle
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where the LF3620 part carries three adjustments: Part discount (−10%), Fleet discount (−5%), Parts Handling Fee (+$3.75).
column6:
1. Go to the Lines tab and locate the LF3620 part.
2. Observe how many adjustment rows show by default.
3. Click 'Show 2 more'.
4. Observe the toggle label after expanding.
column7:
1. By default only the first adjustment row shows (S3-R15).
2. A 'Show 2 more' toggle is shown (N = number of adjustments after the first; S3-R16).
3. Clicking it reveals the remaining two adjustment rows.
4. The toggle label changes to 'Show less' when expanded (S3-R16).

column1: Verify the per-line Total column shows the line's gross total plus its own adjustment amounts (display only)
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where the LF3620 part has base total $58.47 plus adjustments −$6.49, −$2.92, +$3.75.
column6:
1. Go to the Lines tab and locate the LF3620 part.
2. Read the part's Total column, which stacks the base total and each adjustment amount.
3. Note any changes to stored line prices.
column7:
1. The Total column stacks the base total ($58.47) and each adjustment row (−$6.49, −$2.92, +$3.75), so the shown total matches the adjustment rows (S3-R18).
2. The per-line Total is display-only and changes no stored value (S3-R19).

column1: Verify each inline adjustment row has a hover 3-dot Edit/Delete menu when the WO is open with change permission
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with at least one inline line-level adjustment.
column6:
1. Hover an inline adjustment row.
2. Open its ⋯ menu.
column7:
1. A 3-dot menu appears on the right on hover (S12-R5).
2. The menu offers 'Edit' and 'Delete' (S3-R17).
3. The menu is only shown when the WO is open and the user has the change permission.

column1: Verify the Stats tab shows a 'Fees & Discounts (N)' breakdown with Value/% and Amount columns
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with 5 adjustments across scopes is open.
column6:
1. Open the work order's Stats tab.
2. Locate the 'Fees & Discounts (N)' section.
3. Read the column headers and each row.
column7:
1. A 'Fees & Discounts (5)' section is shown; N = count of all adjustments of any scope (S4-R1).
2. Two value columns are shown — a '%' column and an 'Amount' column (S4-R2). (The design mockup labels these 'Value' and 'Amount'.)
3. Each row shows the name, signed rate in the '%'/'Value' column, and the signed resolved amount in 'Amount' (S4-R3).

column1: Verify each Stats F&D row shows a scope hyperlink naming its target
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order (e.g. S2-13274) with a whole-WO discount and line-level part/labor adjustments.
column6:
1. Open the Stats tab and locate the 'Fees & Discounts' section.
2. Read the scope link on each row.
3. Click a scope link on a line-level adjustment.
column7:
1. A whole-WO adjustment's scope link shows the WO number (e.g. 'S2-13274').
2. A line-level adjustment's scope link names the target, e.g. 'Line 1 · (LF3620) Engine Oil Filter' or 'Line 1 · Service - Perform LOF and inspection'.
3. Clicking a scope link jumps to that scope / opens its breakdown (the 'jump to scope' affordance).

column1: Verify the Stats F&D breakdown Total row equals the signed sum of all resolved amounts, with correct signs
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with adjustments: Work order discount −$857.23, Part discount −$649.00, Fleet discount −$292.00, Parts Handling Fee +$3.75, Line discount −$260.77.
column6:
1. Open the Stats tab 'Fees & Discounts' section.
2. Read the sign in the '%'/'Value' column for a fee vs a discount vs a Flat Amount row.

column7:
1. The template is deleted from the location library.
2. The customer's default link to it is removed (no longer in the customer's Default Fees & Discounts table; tab count decreases).
3. The existing work order's "ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Discount" adjustment REMAINS unchanged.

column1: Verify deleting a customer removes that customer's default links
column5: 1. A disposable ZZAUTOTEST customer has at least 1 default fee/discount linked.
column6:
1. Delete the ZZAUTOTEST customer.
2. Confirm the templates that were its defaults still exist in Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts.
column7:
1. The customer and its default links are removed.
2. The underlying location templates are NOT deleted (only the customer's links go away).

column1: Verify a newly created customer inherits every auto-apply location template as a default
column5: 1. The location has exactly 2 templates marked auto-apply and 1 template not auto-apply.
column6:
1. Create a brand-new customer at this location.
2. Open the new customer's Fees & Discounts tab.
column7:
1. The 2 auto-apply templates are already present as defaults (tab reads "Fees & Discounts (2)").
2. The non-auto-apply template is NOT added as a default.

column1: Verify the customer Fees & Discounts tab and controls are hidden without the required permissions
column5: 1. A ZZAUTOTEST role is assigned to Tech (exact-user-match) with Customer Management: Create & Edit ON but Manage Accounts Payable and Receivable OFF.
