3. Restore Tech to the Time Clock role afterward.
column7:
1. Without Manage AP/AR, the customer "Fees & Discounts" tab and its controls are hidden entirely.
2. Both Customer Management: Create & Edit AND Manage AP/AR are required to view/change customer defaults; missing either hides the tab/controls.

column1: Verify a template that is both location auto-apply AND a customer default is added only ONCE to a new WO
column5: 1. A template "ZZAUTOTEST Env Fee" is marked auto-apply at the location AND is a default on the test customer.
column6:
1. Create a NEW work order for the customer.
2. Open the WO Fees & Discounts card and count how many "ZZAUTOTEST Env Fee" adjustments appear.
column7:
1. Exactly ONE "ZZAUTOTEST Env Fee" adjustment appears on the new work order.
2. No second copy of the same template's adjustment is added — the single add is the settled intended behavior (a duplicate would be a defect).

column1: Verify add/remove/load failure on customer defaults shows the standard error notification
column2: API — Customer Fees & Discounts tab — negative
column5: 1. A way to force a server error (e.g., simulate a network/API failure) on the add or remove call.
column6:
1. On the customer Fees & Discounts tab, trigger an add or remove while the backend call fails.
2. Observe the feedback.
column7:
1. The system shows its STANDARD error notification (no custom per-action string).
2. The default list is not corrupted (the failed action is not partially applied).

column1: Verify the location template library lives at Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts, below Canned Lines
column5: 1. You have Settings → Finance access.
column6:
1. Go to Administration → Finance.
2. Locate the Fees & Discounts section.
column7:
1. A "Fees & Discounts" template page/section is present under Administration → Finance (route /administration/adjustment-templates).
2. It appears directly below "Payment Methods".

column1: Verify the template list columns and the delete action
column5: 1. The location has at least 1 template.
column6:
1. Open Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts.
2. Read the table column headers and row controls.
column7:
1. Columns left to right: Name, Type, Calculation Type, Amount, Max Amount, Taxable, "Auto-Apply To Work Orders", and a delete action.
2. Column headers are bold; cells are plain text.
3. Each row has a delete control.

column1: Verify creating a Fee template (dialog fields, confirm button, success toast)
column5: 1. You are on Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts.
column6:
1. Click "New fee / discount".
2. Confirm the dialog title reads "New Fee / Discount".
3. Set Type = "Fee"; Calculation type = "% of Labor Total"; Name = "ZZAUTOTEST Shop Fee"; Percent = 5; leave Max Amount blank; leave the Taxable toggle ON; optionally add a Description; leave the "Auto-apply to new work orders" toggle OFF.
4. Click the confirm button.
column7:
1. The dialog has fields: Type (Fee/Discount/Processing Fee dropdown), Calculation type, Name (up to 100 chars), "$ Default Amount"/Percent, "Max Amount (Optional)" (percentage methods only), a Taxable toggle (default ON), a "Description (Optional)" field (up to 255 chars), and an "Auto-apply to new work orders" toggle.
2. There is NO scope field (every template is whole-WO).
3. The confirm button reads exactly "Create".
4. On save, a success toast reads exactly "Template created" and the new template appears in the list.

column1: Verify creating a Discount template shows the "Discount added" toast
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts page.
column6:
1. Click "New fee / discount".
2. Set Type = "Discount"; Calculation type = "% of Subtotal"; Name = "ZZAUTOTEST Loyalty"; Percent = 8; set the Taxable toggle OFF.
3. Click "Create".
column7:
1. Save succeeds and the toast reads exactly "Template created" (a generic message, not a per-type "Discount added").
2. The template list shows "ZZAUTOTEST Loyalty", Type Discount, Calculation Type % of Subtotal, Amount −8%, Taxable No.

column1: Verify the auto-apply checkbox adds the template to every new WO at that location
column5: 1. You can create a template and then a new work order at the same location.
column6:
1. Create a template "ZZAUTOTEST Auto Fee" (Fee, Flat Amount, $10.00, taxable) with "Auto-apply to all new work orders at this location" CHECKED.
2. Create a NEW work order at that location.
3. Open the WO Fees & Discounts card.
column7:
1. The auto-apply checkbox is labeled exactly "Auto-apply to all new work orders at this location".
2. The new WO automatically carries a Whole Work Order Fee "ZZAUTOTEST Auto Fee" = +$10.00.
3. The added adjustment copies the template's name, type, method, amount, taxable, Max Amount as of WO creation.

column1: Verify editing a template (open by row click, "Save" button, update toast)
column5: 1. A Fee template "ZZAUTOTEST Shop Fee" exists.
column6:
1. On the admin Fees & Discounts page, click the "ZZAUTOTEST Shop Fee" row.
2. Confirm the dialog title reads "Edit Fee / Discount".
3. Change the Percent from 5 to 7 and click the confirm button.
column7:
1. Clicking the row opens the edit dialog titled "Edit Fee / Discount".
2. The confirm button reads exactly "Save" (edit mode); Type and Calculation type are locked (read-only) in template edit.
3. On save, the toast reads exactly "Template updated" and the list shows the new 7% value.

column1: Verify the template delete confirm dialog copy and buttons
column5: 1. A template that is NOT a default for any customer exists.
column6:
1. On the admin Fees & Discounts page, click the delete action on the template.
2. Read the confirm dialog.
column7:
1. The confirm dialog message reads exactly "Are you sure you want to delete this fee / discount?"
2. It has a red "Delete" confirm button and a Cancel button.
3. Confirming removes the template from the list.

column1: Verify the delete confirm adds a warning when the template is a default for one or more customers
column5: 1. A template is set as a default for exactly 2 customers.
column6:
1. On the admin Fees & Discounts page, click the delete action on that template.
2. Read the confirm dialog.
column7:
1. The standardized "Delete Template" confirmation dialog opens (the same standardized delete confirmation used elsewhere in Settings, e.g. for pricing matrices).
2. The dialog includes the warning: "This template is set as a default for 2 customer(s). Deleting it will remove it from them." — the number reflects how many customers currently have the template as a default.

column1: Verify deleting a template leaves work-order adjustments made from it unchanged
column5: 1. A template has been applied to an OPEN work order as an adjustment.
column6:
1. Delete the template from Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts (confirm).
2. Open the work order and check the WO Fees & Discounts card.
column7:
1. The template is removed from the library.
2. The work order's adjustment made from that template REMAINS unchanged (same name, amount, taxable).

column1: Verify template scoping — labour-method templates only appear in labour modals, parts-method only in parts modals
column5:
1. The location has: a "% of Labor Total" template, a "% of Parts Total" template, and a Flat Amount template.
2. A work order with at least one labor line and one part exists.
column6:
1. On a labor line's 3-dot menu, choose "Add Fee / Discount" and open the "Apply from template (optional)" picker.
2. Note which templates are offered, and the compatibility hint.
3. Cancel; on a part's menu choose "Add Fee / Discount" and open the same picker.
4. Note which templates are offered.
column7:
1. From the labor line, the picker lists only Flat Amount and "% of Labor Total" templates (the "% of Parts Total" template is NOT offered).
2. From the part, the picker lists only Flat Amount and "% of Parts Total" templates (the "% of Labor Total" template is NOT offered).
3. When filtered, a hint reads exactly "Showing templates compatible with this line."
4. Neither picker lists any Processing Fee template.

column1: Verify Max Amount appears only for percentage methods and 0 is treated as empty
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog.
column6:
1. Set Calculation type = "Flat Amount" and observe whether "Max Amount (Optional)" is shown.
2. Switch Calculation type to "% of Subtotal" and observe again.
3. Enter 0 into Max Amount and save.
column7:
1. For Flat Amount, the "Max Amount (Optional)" field is NOT shown.
2. For a percentage method, "Max Amount (Optional)" IS shown.
3. Entering 0 in Max Amount is treated as empty (no maximum).

column1: Verify the template list empty-state message
column5: 1. The location has zero templates.
column6:
1. Open Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts.
2. Read the empty state.
column7: 1. The page shows exactly "No fees or discounts yet — click Add to create your first."

column1: Verify a percentage-discount template is capped at 100% while a percentage-fee template is uncapped
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog.
column6:
1. Set Type = "Discount", Calculation type = "% of Subtotal", Percent = 150, and try to save.
2. Change Type = "Fee", Percent = 150, and try to save.
column7:
1. The 150% discount is rejected (percentage discounts may not exceed 100%).
2. The 150% fee is accepted (percentage fees have no upper limit).

column1: Verify a Fee/Discount template offers the four whole-WO methods and no scope field
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog with Type = Fee or Discount.
column6:
1. Open the Calculation type dropdown.
2. Look for any scope field.
column7:
1. The Calculation type options for Fee/Discount are: Flat Amount, % of Labor Total, % of Parts Total, % of Subtotal.
2. There is NO Labor Line or Part Line method on a template, and NO scope field (every template is whole-work-order).

column1: Verify the template save-failure toast
column5: 1. A way to force a save failure on the template create/edit call.
column6:
1. Fill a valid template and click save while the backend call fails.
2. Observe feedback.
column7: 1. An error toast reads exactly "There was an error saving the fee / discount. Please try again."

column1: Verify the admin Fees & Discounts page is gated by Settings → Finance
column5: 1. A ZZAUTOTEST role is assigned to Tech (exact-user-match) WITHOUT Settings → Finance.
column6:
1. Log in as Tech and try to reach Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts.
2. Restore Tech to Time Clock afterward.
column7: 1. Per the target model (S13-R8), without Settings → Finance the admin Fees & Discounts page is not accessible (create/edit/delete templates blocked).

column1: Verify template Name enforces the 100-character limit
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog.
column6:
1. Type a 100-character name and observe it is accepted.
2. Attempt to type a 101st character.
column7:
1. Up to 100 characters are accepted.
2. The 101st character is blocked (Name is capped at 100).

column1: Verify "Processing Fee" is a third type in the template builder (template-only)
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog.
column6: 1. Open the Type dropdown in the template create dialog.
column7:
1. The Type dropdown offers three options: "Fee", "Discount", and "Processing Fee".
2. Processing Fee can be created only here (as a template).

column1: Verify a Processing Fee offers only Flat Amount (default) and % of Grand Total, with a tax-inclusive base
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog with Type = "Processing Fee".
column6:
1. Open the Calculation type dropdown while Type = Processing Fee.
2. For comparison, switch Type back to Fee and open the dropdown.
column7:
1. With Type = Processing Fee, Calculation type offers only "Flat Amount" (default) and "% of Grand Total".
2. "% of Grand Total" is offered ONLY for a Processing Fee (it does not appear for Fee/Discount).
3. Per §5-R4, "% of Grand Total" uses a base that includes tax on purpose (net subtotal + tax on that net subtotal) — the one exception to the before-tax rule.

column1: Verify the Max Amount field is hidden for every Processing Fee (both methods)
column5: 1. On the admin create dialog with Type = Processing Fee.
column6:
1. Set Calculation type = Flat Amount and check for a Max Amount field.
2. Set Calculation type = % of Grand Total and check again.
column7: 1. No "Max Amount (Optional)" field is shown for a Processing Fee under either method.

column1: Verify the Processing Fee Taxable control defaults Yes and renders the legal disclosure
column5: 1. On the admin create dialog with Type = Processing Fee.
column6:
1. Observe the Taxable control default value.
2. Read the disclosure text rendered below the Taxable setting.
3. Capture the literal disclosure wording (screenshot).
column7:
1. Taxable is a Yes/No dropdown defaulting to "Yes".
2. A legal disclosure renders below the Taxable setting.
3. The disclosure text must render EXACTLY as written (no paraphrase / auto-translate without legal sign-off).

column1: Verify a Processing Fee cannot be added to a work order by hand
column5:
1. A Processing Fee template exists.
2. An open work order is available.
column6:
1. On the WO toolbar ⋯ menu, choose "Add Work Order Fee / Discount" and open the Type dropdown.
2. Open the "Apply from template (optional)" picker in the same dialog and from a labor line and a part dialog.
column7:
1. The WO Add dialog Type dropdown does NOT list "Processing Fee" (only Fee and Discount).
2. The template picker does NOT list any Processing Fee template from any starting place (WO, labor line, part).

column1: Verify a Processing Fee reaches a new work order via location auto-apply
column5: 1. A Processing Fee template "ZZAUTOTEST Proc Fee" (Flat Amount $5.00, taxable Yes) is marked auto-apply.
column6:
1. Create a NEW work order at that location.
2. Open the WO Fees & Discounts card.
column7:
1. The new WO carries a whole-WO Processing Fee "ZZAUTOTEST Proc Fee" = +$5.00.
2. The card entry offers "Delete" only (no "Edit") for the Processing Fee.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee reaches a new work order via a customer default
column5: 1. A Processing Fee template is set as a default on the test customer.
column6:
1. Create a NEW work order for that customer.
2. Open the WO Fees & Discounts card.
column7:
1. The new WO carries the Processing Fee as a whole-WO adjustment (independent copy).
2. On the WO it offers Delete only (no Edit).

column1: Verify a Processing Fee on a WO can be removed but not edited
column5: 1. An open WO carries a Processing Fee (via auto-apply or customer default).
column6:
1. Hover the Processing Fee entry in the WO Fees & Discounts card and open its 3-dot menu.
2. Note the available actions, then attempt to remove it.
column7:
1. The entry's menu shows "Edit" and "Remove"; the Edit control is inert for a Processing Fee — attempting to edit it is rejected by the system (a Processing Fee cannot be edited on the WO instance).
2. Removing it works normally (opens the "Remove Fee / Discount" confirm and removes on confirm).
3. To change amount/method/taxable you must edit the TEMPLATE, not the WO instance.

column1: Verify a % of Grand Total Processing Fee resolves last on a tax-inclusive base (3% of $324 → +$9.72)
column5:
1. A Processing Fee template "ZZAUTOTEST 3% Proc" (% of Grand Total, 3%, taxable Yes) auto-applies.
2. A work order exists whose net subtotal (after line-level adjustments) = $300.00 and pre-fee tax = $24.00 (so Grand Total base = $324.00).
column6:
1. Open the work order and read the Processing Fee resolved amount.
2. Check the resolve order relative to other adjustments.
column7:
1. The Processing Fee resolves to +$9.72 (3% × $324.00).
2. It resolves LAST (Step 3), excluded from its own base and from every other Processing Fee's base.
3. If taxable, its $9.72 is added to the taxable amount (final tax grows by tax on $9.72) but the $324.00 base does NOT change (no feedback loop).

column1: Verify a Processing Fee with a Max Amount or a disallowed method is rejected
column5: 1. Ability to submit template data (via UI edge case or API) for a Processing Fee carrying a Max Amount, or a method other than Flat Amount / % of Grand Total.
column6:
1. Attempt to save a Processing Fee template that carries a Max Amount.
2. Attempt to save a Processing Fee with a method other than Flat Amount or % of Grand Total (e.g. % of Subtotal).
column7:
1. Both attempts are REJECTED by the system.
2. A Processing Fee may only be Flat Amount or % of Grand Total and never carries a Max Amount.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee always adds to the total (never a discount)
column5: 1. A Processing Fee template exists and is on a WO.
column6:
1. On the admin dialog, confirm there is no way to make a Processing Fee a discount.
2. On the WO, confirm the resolved amount carries a plus (+) sign.
column7:
1. A Processing Fee always resolves to a plus (+) amount; it can never be a discount.
2. There is no "Processing Discount" type.

column1: Verify editing a Processing Fee template does not change Processing Fees already on existing WOs
column5: 1. A Processing Fee template auto-applied to an existing OPEN work order (e.g. Flat $5.00).
column6:
1. Edit the Processing Fee template amount from $5.00 to $8.00 and save.
2. Open the existing work order and read the Processing Fee amount.
column7:
1. The existing WO's Processing Fee STILL shows $5.00 (unchanged).
2. Only NEW work orders created after the edit pick up the $8.00 value.

column1: Verify multiple Processing Fees each exclude ALL Processing Fees' amounts and tax from the shared base
column5:
1. Two Processing Fee templates (both % of Grand Total) auto-apply to one work order.
2. Net subtotal $300.00, pre-fee tax $24.00 → Grand Total base $324.00.
column6:
1. Create a new WO so both Processing Fees apply.
2. Read each Processing Fee's resolved amount.
column7:
1. Both Processing Fees resolve against the SAME $324.00 base (which excludes every Processing Fee's amount and tax).
2. Neither Processing Fee grows the other's base.

column1: Verify the system rejects a Processing Fee carrying a minimum amount
column5: 1. Ability to submit a Processing Fee with a non-empty minimum amount (no UI control exists; guard for external data).
column6: 1. Submit a Processing Fee template that carries a minimum amount value.
column7: 1. The system rejects it (a Processing Fee must not carry a minimum amount).

column1: Verify one layout renders adjustments on both the estimate and the invoice
column5: 1. A work order has whole-WO and line-level adjustments and can produce both an estimate and an invoice.
column6:
1. View the customer ESTIMATE for the WO and note the adjustment rendering.
2. Invoice the WO and view the customer INVOICE.
column7:
1. Both the estimate and the invoice show the same adjustment layout.
2. Adjustments appear on both whenever present.

column1: Verify a labor-line percentage adjustment renders indented with ↳, the "(% of labor)" phrase, and correct amount sign
column5: 1. A WO has a labor line with a "Shop Supply Fee" (% of Labor Total, fee) and a labor-line discount.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Find the labor line and its adjustment rows.
column7:
1. The adjustment shows indented UNDER its labor line with a "↳" arrow before the name.
2. For the percentage fee the name is followed by the phrase "(% of labor)" (a phrase, not a number).
3. A fee amount shows as "$X.XX"; a discount amount shows in accounting brackets "($X.XX)" — two decimals, no minus sign.

column1: Verify a part-line adjustment renders with "(% of parts)" (percentage) and no phrase for Flat Amount
column5: 1. A WO part has a percentage part-line adjustment and another part has a Flat Amount part-line adjustment.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Inspect both part-line adjustment rows.
column7:
1. The percentage part-line adjustment shows the phrase "(% of parts)" after its name.
2. The Flat Amount adjustment shows NO bracketed phrase.

column1: Verify fee vs discount amount formatting (fee "$X.XX", discount "($X.XX)")
column5: 1. A WO has both a fee and a discount adjustment.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Compare the fee and discount amount cells (both per-line and in the bottom Adjustments block).
column7:
1. A fee amount reads "$X.XX" (e.g. "$3.75").
2. A discount amount reads "($X.XX)" in round accounting brackets (e.g. "($26.08)") — two decimals and NO minus sign.
3. Both the per-line rows and the bottom Adjustments block use the same format.

column1: Verify the bottom "Adjustments" block lists whole-WO adjustments one by one in creation order
column5: 1. A WO has 3 whole-WO adjustments created in a known order, including a % of Subtotal and a Flat Amount.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Find the "Adjustments" block near the bottom and read the order and labels.
column7:
1. A block titled "Adjustments" appears after Labor/Parts/Shop Supplies and before Subtotal (then Tax, then Total).
2. Whole-WO adjustments are listed one by one in CREATION order (oldest first).
3. Each percentage adjustment shows its phrase — one of "% of labor", "% of parts", "% of subtotal", or "% of grand total" (Processing Fee); a Flat Amount shows no phrase.

column1: Verify line-level adjustments are grouped by name+type in the bottom block with a "(×N)" count
column5: 1. A WO has three separate "Shop Supply Fee" line-level fees (same name+type) across different lines.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Inspect the bottom "Adjustments" block.
column7:
1. The three same-named line-level fees are grouped into ONE row reading "Shop Supply Fee (×3)" with the total resolved amount.
2. Each of the three ALSO still shows inline under its own target line (S5-R8).

column1: Verify a % of Grand Total Processing Fee shows the "% of grand total" phrase on the document
column5: 1. A WO carries a % of Grand Total Processing Fee.
column6: 1. View the customer estimate/invoice bottom Adjustments block.
column7: 1. The Processing Fee row shows the phrase "% of grand total" after its name.

column1: Verify Shop Supplies is hidden on the estimate/invoice/financial tab when the total is $0.00
column5: 1. A WO whose total shop supplies = $0.00.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate, the invoice, and the financial tab.
2. Look for a Shop Supplies heading/line.
3. Also open the WO's left-side financial card.
column7:
1. When shop supplies = $0.00, the Shop Supplies header/contents do NOT display on the estimate, invoice, or financial tab.
2. Shop Supplies remains visible/modifiable in the WO left-side financial card (hidden only from the end-customer views).

column1: Verify Shop Supplies reappears on the customer views when its total becomes greater than $0.00
column5: 1. A WO that currently has $0.00 shop supplies (Shop Supplies hidden on customer views).
column6:
1. Add shop supplies so the total becomes > $0.00.
2. Re-view the estimate/invoice/financial tab.
column7: 1. Once shop supplies > $0.00, the Shop Supplies heading and contents become visible again on the customer-facing views.

column1: Verify a line-level adjustment on a not-billable (declined) line resolves to $0.00 but still shows
column5: 1. A WO labor line with an adjustment is set to declined/not-billable.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate (including a Needs Approval estimate).
2. Inspect the declined line's adjustment.
column7:
1. The adjustment resolves to $0.00 while the target is not billable, but still SHOWS wherever its target shows (including a Needs Approval estimate).
2. When the line becomes billable/authorized, the adjustment resolves to its non-zero amount.

column1: Verify the Adjustments block sits after Labor/Parts/Shop Supplies and before Subtotal → Tax → Total
column5: 1. A WO with labor, parts, shop supplies (> $0.00), and whole-WO adjustments.
column6: 1. View the customer estimate/invoice totals section from top to bottom.
column7: 1. Order is: Labor, Parts, Shop Supplies, then the "Adjustments" block, then Subtotal, then Tax, then Total.

column1: Verify each fee/discount exports to QuickBooks as its own invoice line item (fee +, discount −)
column5:
1. Location has an active QuickBooks connection with mapped Fee and Discount items.
2. A WO with one fee (+$10.00) and one discount (−$20.00) is invoiced.
column6:
1. Invoice the WO so it syncs to QuickBooks.
2. Inspect the QuickBooks invoice line items.
column7:
1. The fee is its own QuickBooks line item with a positive amount (+$10.00).
2. The discount is its own QuickBooks line item with a negative amount (−$20.00).
3. Each adjustment is a separate line (not merged into labor/parts).

column1: Verify the QuickBooks line description equals the adjustment name and the item is the mapped Fee/Discount item
column5:
1. QuickBooks connected with a mapped Fee item and Discount item.
2. A WO has a fee named "Hazmat Disposal Fee"; the WO is invoiced.
column6: 1. Inspect the synced QuickBooks line for the fee.
column7:
1. The QuickBooks line DESCRIPTION = "Hazmat Disposal Fee" (the adjustment name as shown on the customer invoice).
2. The Product/Service ITEM = the location's mapped Fee item (not the adjustment name).
3. A discount posts to the mapped Discount item likewise.

column1: Verify a $0.00 resolved adjustment is skipped when sent to QuickBooks
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; a WO has an adjustment that resolves to $0.00 (e.g. target not billable, or $0 base).
column6:
1. Invoice the WO and inspect the QuickBooks line items.
2. Also view the ShopView screens for the same adjustment.
column7:
1. The $0.00 adjustment is NOT sent as a QuickBooks line (skipped).
2. It still SHOWS as $0.00 on every other ShopView screen.

column1: Verify adding a fee is blocked when the Fee item is unmapped (exact message)
column5:
1. QuickBooks connected; the Fee item is NOT mapped in Settings → QuickBooks.
2. The Discount item IS mapped.
3. An open WO is available.
column6:
1. Open the WO toolbar ⋯ → "Add Work Order Fee / Discount", set Type = Fee, and try to save.
2. In the same dialog, set Type = Discount and try to save.
column7:
1. Saving a FEE is blocked with the message exactly: "Map a Fee item in Settings → QuickBooks before adding a fee." ("Settings → QuickBooks" is a link).
2. Saving a DISCOUNT succeeds (the block is per kind — only fees are blocked when the Fee item is missing).

column1: Verify adding a discount is blocked when the Discount item is unmapped (exact message)
column5:
1. QuickBooks connected; the Discount item is NOT mapped; the Fee item IS mapped.
2. An open WO is available.
column6:
1. Try to add a Discount to the WO.
2. Try to add a Fee to the WO.
column7:
1. Saving a DISCOUNT is blocked with the message exactly: "Map a Discount item in Settings → QuickBooks before adding a discount."
2. Saving a FEE succeeds (per-kind block).

column1: Verify the mapping guard blocks adds on every add surface (WO, labor line, part, part sale, template-apply)
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; Fee item UNMAPPED.
column6: 1. Try to add a fee from: the WO dialog, a labor-line dialog, a part dialog, a part-sale whole-sale dialog and a single-part dialog, and by applying a fee template to a WO.
column7: 1. Every one of these add paths is blocked with the same "Map a Fee item in Settings → QuickBooks before adding a fee." message.

column1: Verify an auto-apply default cannot be saved while the matching QuickBooks item is unmapped
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; Fee item UNMAPPED.
column6:
1. Try to mark a Fee template as auto-apply at the location.
2. Try to set a Fee template as a customer default.
column7:
1. Setting up an auto-apply Fee default (location auto-apply OR customer default) is BLOCKED while the Fee item is unmapped.
2. The block is at setup, so an auto-apply default never adds a fee on the server without a mapped item.

column1: Verify creating/editing a non-auto-apply template is always allowed and no block exists when QuickBooks is not connected
column5: 1. Scenario A: QuickBooks connected with Fee item unmapped; scenario B: QuickBooks NOT connected.
column6:
1. Scenario A: create/edit a NON-auto-apply Fee template.
2. Scenario B (QuickBooks not connected): add a fee to a WO.
column7:
1. Scenario A: creating/editing a non-auto-apply template in Settings is always allowed (no block).
2. Scenario B: with QuickBooks not connected, there is no mapping block anywhere.

column1: Verify unmapping an in-use item routes affected invoices to Unexported Items (recoverable, no data lost)
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected with mapped Fee item; a WO with a fee is ready to invoice/sync.
column6:
1. Unmap the Fee item in Settings → QuickBooks (or connect QuickBooks after fees already exist).
2. Sync/invoice the affected WO.
3. Re-map the Fee item and re-export the invoice.
column7:
1. At sync time, each affected invoice goes to "Unexported Items" (not hard-blocked).
2. After re-mapping the item and re-exporting, the invoice exports; no data is lost.
3. The Settings → QuickBooks page prompts to map the Fee and Discount items, the same way it prompts for Credit and Deposit items.

column1: Verify a single QuickBooks Class applies to every synced line including fee/discount lines
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected with a location Class set; a WO with fees/discounts is invoiced.
column6: 1. Inspect the synced invoice's line items and their Class.
column7:
1. The one location Class applies to every synced line, including fee and discount lines (not split/allocated).
2. If no Class is set, synced lines carry no class.

column1: Verify a deleted/deactivated Class aborts the entire invoice sync (no substitution)
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; the location's Class has been deleted/deactivated in QuickBooks.
column6: 1. Attempt to sync an invoice with fees/discounts.
column7:
1. The entire invoice sync ABORTS (validation fails on the class).
2. The class is NOT substituted with another.

column1: Verify the net subtotal floors at $0.00 with the $100/$10/$150 worked example (non-taxable vs taxable discount)
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; a WO has $100.00 taxable parts and $10.00 tax.
column6:
1. Add a NON-taxable $150.00 discount to the WO; observe the net subtotal, tax, and total.
2. In a second WO with the same base, add a TAXABLE $150.00 discount instead; observe tax and total.
column7:
1. Non-taxable $150.00 discount: net subtotal −$50.00 floors to $0.00; because the discount is non-taxable, tax stays $10.00; the customer pays $10.00 (total equals the tax, not $0.00). The $50.00 excess is carried as a customer credit.
2. Taxable $150.00 discount: it lowers the taxable amount to $0.00, so tax = $0.00 and the customer pays $0.00.
3. The floor applies only to the pre-tax net subtotal, never below $0.00; tax is computed on top of the floored subtotal.

column1: Verify discount lines to QuickBooks are capped with largest-remainder whole-cent penny allocation
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; a WO where stacked MULTIPLE discount lines drive the net subtotal below $0.00 (floor applies).
column6:
1. Invoice/sync the WO.
2. Inspect the discount line amounts sent to QuickBooks.
column7:
1. The discount lines are capped so they sum exactly to the floored net subtotal and never fall below it.
2. With multiple discount lines, the cap is split proportionally to each line's size, allocated in WHOLE cents via the largest-remainder method (no fractional cent, no negative total).
3. The amount removed by the cap becomes the carried customer credit.

column1: Verify a mandatory warn/confirm before saving when discounts exceed the net subtotal
column5: 1. A WO where discounts will exceed the net subtotal.
column6:
1. Add discounts that push the net subtotal below $0.00.
2. Attempt to save the WO.
column7:
1. Before the WO can be saved, the user is WARNED that the net subtotal will floor at $0.00, tax on the taxable base is still owed, and the excess (shown as a dollar amount) will be carried as a customer credit.
2. The user must CONFIRM; the carry is never silent.

column1: Verify the excess is recorded as a customer credit and posts to QuickBooks as a tax-exempt goodwill credit memo
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; a WO where the floor applied (with a $50.00 excess carried as credit).
column6:
1. After confirming the over-discount, check the customer's Deposits & Credits.
2. Inspect the QuickBooks posting for the carried credit.
column7:
1. The floored-off amount ($50.00 in the worked example) is recorded as a freestanding customer credit not tied to a WO; it carries forward and is applied to the customer's next invoice.
2. In QuickBooks it posts as a goodwill credit memo on the location's Customer Credit item, marked tax-exempt.
3. It is NOT a QuickBooks payment (no cash received).

column1: Verify a synced line's tax follows the adjustment's taxable setting
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; a WO has one taxable fee and one non-taxable fee; the WO is invoiced.
column6: 1. Inspect the synced QuickBooks lines for both fees.
column7:
1. The taxable fee's line carries the invoice's active tax.
2. The non-taxable fee's line carries zero tax.

column1: Verify one history entry per add/edit/remove with the correct bold event labels
column5: 1. You have Work Orders: Create and Edit and can add/edit/remove adjustments on an open WO.
column6:
1. Add a Fee to the WO, then edit it, then remove it.
2. Add a Discount to the WO, then edit it, then remove it.
3. Open the WO history log.
column7:
1. Each add, each edit, and each remove records exactly ONE entry.
2. Fee events read (bold): "Fee added", "Fee updated", "Fee removed".
3. Discount events read (bold): "Discount added", "Discount updated", "Discount removed".

column1: Verify the history detail block shows Name, Type, Amount (set rate), and Applied-to label
column5: 1. A WO has (a) a whole-WO 10% fee named "Env Fee", (b) a labor-line $5.00 flat fee, (c) a part-line discount.
column6:
1. Add each of the three adjustments and open the history log.
2. Read the details block for each entry.
column7:
1. Name shows the adjustment name (e.g. "Env Fee").
2. Type shows "Fee" or "Discount".
3. Amount shows the SET RATE, not the resolved total — "$X.XX" for Flat (e.g. "$5.00") or "X.XX%" for percentage (e.g. "10.00%"), with no +/− sign.
4. Applied to shows "Full invoice" (whole WO), "Labor line", or "Part" respectively.

column1: Verify an adjustment entry leaves the saved-state icon empty and the Line column shows "−"
column5: 1. A WO has at least one whole-WO adjustment and one line-level adjustment logged.
column6: 1. Open the WO history log and inspect the saved-state icon column and the Line column for adjustment entries.
column7:
1. The saved-state icon column is EMPTY for every adjustment entry.
2. The Line column shows "−" for every adjustment entry regardless of scope (no line number, even for line-level adjustments).

column1: Verify fee/discount history stays visible when the F&D UI is hidden by the Fees & Discounts feature
column5:
1. A WO already has fee/discount history entries.
2. The Fees & Discounts feature is then turned OFF for the org.
column6:
1. With the flag OFF, confirm no F&D controls render on the WO.
2. Open the WO history log.
column7:
1. All F&D controls are hidden (flag off).
2. The previously recorded fee/discount history entries STILL show in the history log.

column1: Verify F&D history stays visible when the F&D UI is hidden by See Financial Data being off
column5:
1. A WO has fee/discount history entries.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST role is assigned to Tech with Work Orders: Create and Edit ON but See Financial Data OFF (exact-user-match).
column6:
1. Log in as Tech and open the WO — confirm dollar amounts are hidden on the F&D surfaces.
2. Open the WO history log.
3. Restore Tech to Time Clock afterward.
column7:
1. Fee/discount dollar amounts are hidden on the normal F&D surfaces (SFD off).
2. The fee/discount history entries STILL show in the history log (the log shows the SET rate, not a resolved total, so SFD does not gate it).

column1: Verify fee/discount history entries are gated by Work Orders: Create and Edit (WO log) and Work Order Lines: Create and Edit (line history)
column5:
1. A WO has fee/discount history.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST role is assigned to Tech WITHOUT Work Orders: Create and Edit and WITHOUT Work Order Lines: Create and Edit (exact-user-match).
column6:
1. Log in as Tech and attempt to view the WO history log and an individual labor-line / part-line history.
2. Restore Tech to Time Clock afterward.
column7: 1. Without Work Orders: Create and Edit, the WO history log (including fee/discount entries) is not accessible; viewing an individual labor-line or part-line history requires Work Order Lines: Create and Edit.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee is logged as a fee with "Full invoice" applied-to and no "updated" entry
column5: 1. A WO carries a Processing Fee (via auto-apply or customer default).
column6:
1. Confirm the Processing Fee was added (auto) and then remove it from the WO.
2. Open the WO history log and read the Processing Fee entries.
column7:
1. The add logs event "Fee added" and the remove logs "Fee removed" (Type shown as "Fee").
2. Applied to shows "Full invoice".
3. There is NO "Fee updated" entry for a Processing Fee (it can't be edited on a WO).

column1: Verify an edit that changes the rate records the new set rate (not the resolved total)
column5: 1. A WO has a whole-WO 10% fee.
column6:
1. Edit the fee's percent from 10% to 15% and save.
2. Open the history log and read the "Fee updated" entry's Amount detail.
column7: 1. The "Fee updated" entry's Amount shows "15.00%" (the new SET rate), not the resolved dollar total.

column1: Verify a percentage adjustment resolves as base × percent (10% fee on $150.00 → +$15.00)
column5:
1. You are signed in with a role that has See Financial Data and Work Orders: Create and Edit.
2. An open work order (not Invoiced/Paid, not in history mode) exists whose relevant base equals exactly $150.00 (e.g. net labor total = $150.00). Mark any throwaway data ZZAUTOTEST.
column6:
1. Open the work order.
2. From the work-order toolbar ⋯ (more) menu choose "Add Work Order Fee / Discount".
3. Set Type = Fee.
4. Set Calculation type to a percentage method whose base is $150.00 (e.g. % of Labor Total with net labor = $150.00).
5. Enter Percent = 10.
6. Save with "Add Fee".
column7:
1. Input: base = $150.00, rate = 10% fee.
2. Resolved amount = $150.00 × 0.10 = +$15.00 exactly.
3. The adjustment shows a signed rate badge "+10%" and resolved amount "+$15.00" in plain grey on the WO sidebar card / line table.

column1: Verify percentage rounding — half a cent or more rounds UP (5% discount on $33.33 → $1.6665 → −$1.67)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and Work Orders: Create and Edit.
2. An open work order whose target base equals exactly $33.33.
column6:
1. Open the work order.
2. Start an adjustment against the $33.33 base.
3. Set Type = Discount, Calculation type = a percentage method on that base.
4. Enter Percent = 5.
5. Save.
column7:
1. Input: base = $33.33, rate = 5% discount.
2. Raw = $33.33 × 0.05 = $1.6665.
3. Because the third decimal is ≥ half a cent, it rounds UP: resolved = −$1.67 (not −$1.66).
4. Sign is minus (discount).

column1: Verify a Flat Amount on Whole-WO or Labor Line resolves to the set amount exactly (no quantity multiplier)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data plus the matching change permission.
2. An open work order with at least one labor line.
column6:
1. Open the work order.
2. Add a Whole-WO fee: toolbar ⋯ → Add Work Order Fee / Discount, Type = Fee, Calculation type = Flat Amount, Amount = $25.00, save.
3. Add a Labor Line discount: on a labor line's 3-dot menu → Add Fee / Discount, Type = Discount, Calculation type = Flat Amount, Amount = $10.00, save.
column7:
1. Whole-WO Flat fee resolves to exactly +$25.00 (no quantity part).
2. Labor Line Flat discount resolves to exactly −$10.00 (Labor Line Flat has no quantity part, §5-R14).
3. Neither amount is multiplied by any quantity.

column1: Verify a Flat Amount on a Part Line is PER ITEM (amount × quantity: $5.00 × qty 3 → −$15.00; qty 1 → −$5.00)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and Work Order Lines: Create and Edit.
2. An open work order with a part whose quantity = 3.
column6:
1. Open the work order.
2. On the part's menu choose "Add Fee / Discount" (locks Part Line scope).
3. Set Type = Discount, Calculation type = Flat Amount, Amount = $5.00, save.
4. Change the part quantity from 3 to 1 and observe the adjustment re-resolve.
column7:
1. Input: Flat $5.00 discount on a part with qty 3.
2. Resolved = $5.00 × 3 = −$15.00.
3. After quantity changes to 1, resolved re-computes to −$5.00 ($5.00 × 1).

column1: Verify a percentage discount cannot exceed 100% (fee percentages have no upper limit)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order.
column6:
1. Open the Add Fee / Discount dialog at any scope.
2. Set Type = Discount, Calculation type = a percentage method.
3. Enter Percent = 101 and attempt to save.
4. Change Percent = 100 and save.
5. Repeat with Type = Fee and Percent = 150; save.
column7:
1. Discount at 101% is rejected (invalid) — a percentage discount may not exceed 100% (§5-R2).
2. Discount at exactly 100% is allowed.
3. Fee at 150% is allowed — percentage fees have no upper limit.

column1: Verify minimum values — Flat Amount smallest is $0.01, Percentage smallest is 0.01%
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order.
column6:
1. Open the Add Fee / Discount dialog.
2. With Calculation type = Flat Amount, try Amount = $0.00 (blocked), then Amount = $0.01 (allowed); save.
3. With Calculation type = a percentage method, try Percent = 0 (blocked), then Percent = 0.01 (allowed); save.
column7:
1. Values must be greater than 0 (§5-R1).
2. Flat Amount below $0.01 is invalid; $0.01 is the smallest accepted.
3. Percentage below 0.01% is invalid; 0.01% is the smallest accepted.

column1: Verify Max Amount clamps a percentage result (20% fee on $100 → $20 → Max $15 → +$15.00)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order whose target base = $100.00.
column6:
1. Open the Add Fee / Discount dialog on the $100.00 base.
2. Set Type = Fee, Calculation type = a percentage method.
3. Enter Percent = 20.
4. Enter Max Amount = $15.00.
5. Save.
column7:
1. Uncapped result would be $100.00 × 20% = $20.00.
2. $20.00 exceeds the $15.00 cap, so it is lowered to the cap: resolved = +$15.00.
3. Max Amount only shows for percentage methods (never Flat Amount, never Processing Fee).

column1: Verify Max Amount = $0 forces resolve to $0.00, while blank/empty Max Amount means no cap
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order whose target base = $100.00.
3. Note: a $0 Max Amount can normally only come from old data — an entered 0 is treated as empty in the current dialogs (S2-R25).
column6:
1. Open the Add dialog, Type = Fee, percentage method, Percent = 50 on the $100.00 base.
2. Leave Max Amount blank; save. Observe resolved amount.
3. (Old-data / negative case) With a Max Amount of $0 present, observe resolved amount.
column7:
1. Blank Max Amount = no maximum → resolved = +$50.00 ($100 × 50%).
2. An entered 0 in Max Amount is treated as empty (no maximum) in the dialog (§5-R6, S2-R25) — so it does NOT force $0 when typed in the UI.
3. A genuine Max Amount = $0 (only possible from old data) forces the resolve to $0.00 (§5-R6 example: 50% fee on $100 → $50 → Max $0 → $0.00).

column1: Verify a $0.00 base resolves to $0.00 and the $0.00 line is skipped in QuickBooks (still shown on screens)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order with a target line whose base is $0.00 (e.g. a declined/not-billable labor line, §5-R12).
column6:
1. Add a 15% fee (or any adjustment) against the $0.00 base line.
2. Observe the resolved amount on the WO sidebar card, line table, Stats tab, Financial Info card.
3. Invoice the WO (with an active QuickBooks connection) and observe what syncs.
column7:
1. Resolved amount against a $0.00 base = $0.00 (e.g. 15% fee on $0.00 → $0.00, §5-R3/R8).
2. The $0.00 adjustment SHOWS as $0.00 on every WO screen.
3. In QuickBooks the $0.00 line is SKIPPED — not sent as an invoice line item (§5-R8 / S6-R1).

column1: Verify a negative base is treated as $0 (resolved amount = $0.00, base never goes below zero)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order where an earlier discount has already driven a net total to or below $0 for a whole-WO percentage base.
column6:
1. On a base that would compute negative (e.g. net parts total already floored), add a percentage fee/discount referencing that base.
2. Observe the resolved amount.
column7:
1. If the base is below $0, the system uses $0 as the base (§5-R3, §5-R4: "No base goes below $0").
2. Resolved amount = $0.00.
3. The base is never allowed to go negative for calculation purposes.

column1: Verify a taxable fee raises the taxable amount, a taxable discount lowers it, and a non-taxable adjustment does not change tax
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order for a taxable customer with a known tax rate and a taxable base.
column6:
1. Note the WO's current taxable amount and tax.
2. Add a whole-WO fee with Taxable = Yes; save and note the new taxable amount/tax.
3. Remove it. Add a whole-WO discount with Taxable = Yes; save and note taxable amount/tax.
4. Remove it. Add a whole-WO fee with Taxable = No; save and note taxable amount/tax.
column7:
1. Taxable fee: the taxable amount INCREASES by the fee amount, so tax increases accordingly.
2. Taxable discount: the taxable amount DECREASES by the discount amount, so tax decreases.
3. Non-taxable adjustment: the taxable amount and tax are UNCHANGED (§5-R11).

column1: Verify the 3-step resolution ORDER — line-level on gross first, whole-WO on net second, no stacking within a step
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data plus both change permissions.
2. An open work order with gross labor = $200.00 and gross parts = $100.00 (spec worked example).
column6:
1. Step 1 — add a Labor Line 10% discount on the $200 labor line.
2. Step 2 — add a whole-WO 5% fee using % of Labor Total, and a whole-WO 10% discount using % of Parts Total.
3. Observe each resolved amount and the running net totals.
column7:
1. Step 1 (line-level, on gross): 10% × $200 = −$20.00 → net labor = $180.00.
2. Step 2 (whole-WO, on net from Step 1): 5% fee × $180 net labor = +$9.00; 10% discount × $100 net parts = −$10.00.
3. The two Step-2 adjustments do NOT change each other's base (no stacking within a step).
4. Order is enforced: line-level always resolves before whole-WO.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee resolves LAST on the tax-inclusive Grand Total (3% of $324 → +$9.72)
column5:
1. Role has Settings → Finance to create the template and See Financial Data to view amounts.
2. A Processing Fee template exists: Type = Processing Fee, Calculation type = % of Grand Total, Percent = 3%, marked auto-apply or set as a customer default (a Processing Fee cannot be added to a WO by hand, S8-R16).
3. An open work order whose net subtotal after line discounts = $300.00 with pre-fee tax = $24.00 (Grand Total base = $324.00).
column6:
1. Create the WO so the auto-apply / customer-default Processing Fee is added.
2. Confirm the Processing Fee is present as a whole-WO adjustment on the sidebar card.
3. Observe its resolved amount and confirm it resolves after all line-level and whole-WO adjustments.
column7:
1. Grand Total base = net subtotal $300.00 + tax on that net subtotal $24.00 = $324.00.
2. Processing Fee = 3% × $324.00 = +$9.72.
3. It resolves in Step 3 (last), is excluded from its own base, and does not change any other adjustment's base.

column1: Verify the Processing Fee base includes tax on purpose and never uses a Max Amount
column5:
1. Role has Settings → Finance and See Financial Data.
2. On the template admin page, open the Processing Fee template create/edit dialog.
column6:
1. Create a Processing Fee template with Calculation type = % of Grand Total.
2. Confirm the Max Amount field is not shown for a Processing Fee.
3. Apply it (auto-apply / customer default) to a WO with a taxable Grand Total and check the base used.
4. Mark the Processing Fee taxable = Yes and confirm its own tax does not grow its own base.
column7:
1. Processing Fee % of Grand Total uses a base = net subtotal PLUS the tax on that net subtotal (the one exception to the before-tax rule, §5-R4).
2. No Max Amount field is available for any Processing Fee (S8-R10, S8-N3); saving one with a Max Amount is rejected (S8-N4).
3. A taxable Processing Fee adds its own amount to the taxable amount, but this added tax NEVER changes its own base (no feedback loop, §5-R5).
4. The tax in the base excludes tax from any taxable whole-WO fee/discount and the Processing Fee's own tax.

column1: Verify negative-total floor at $0.00 — non-taxable $150 discount on $100 parts + $10 tax: subtotal floors, customer pays $10, $50 excess → tax-exempt goodwill credit
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order with $100.00 taxable parts and $10.00 tax (spec worked example).
3. Location has an active QuickBooks connection (to verify the credit memo).
column6:
1. Add a whole-WO discount of $150.00 with Taxable = No.
2. Attempt to save and observe the warning/confirm prompt.
3. Confirm, then observe the WO totals.
4. Invoice the WO and observe the QuickBooks postings and the customer's account credit.
column7:
1. Net subtotal = $100.00 − $150.00 = −$50.00 → floored to $0.00 (S6-R10). The floor is on the pre-tax net subtotal only (S6-R10a).
2. Because the discount is non-taxable, tax on the original taxable base is still owed: tax stays $10.00 (S6-R10b).
3. WO total = $10.00 (the tax), not $0.00; customer pays $10.00.
4. Before save, a mandatory warning states the subtotal floors at $0.00, tax is still owed, and the $50.00 excess carries as a customer credit — user must confirm (S6-R12).
5. The $50.00 excess is recorded as a freestanding customer credit not tied to a WO (S6-R11) and posts to QuickBooks as a tax-exempt goodwill credit memo on the Customer Credit item (S6-R13).

column1: Verify a TAXABLE $150 discount on $100 parts drives the taxable amount to $0 → tax $0.00, customer pays $0.00
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order with $100.00 taxable parts and $10.00 tax.
column6:
1. Add a whole-WO discount of $150.00 with Taxable = Yes.
2. Confirm the warning and save.
3. Observe the WO totals.
column7:
1. A taxable $150.00 discount lowers the taxable amount to $0.00.
2. Tax = $0.00 (S6-R10c).
3. Customer pays $0.00 total.
4. By contrast, when the same discount is non-taxable the $10.00 tax is still owed.

column1: Verify multiple discount lines are penny-capped via largest-remainder so capped discounts sum exactly to the floored net subtotal (no negative, whole-cent)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. Location has an active QuickBooks connection.
3. An open work order with a small net subtotal and two or more discount lines whose combined size exceeds it.
column6:
1. Add two (or more) whole-WO discounts whose total exceeds the net subtotal.
2. Confirm the over-discount warning and save.
3. Invoice and inspect the discount line amounts sent to QuickBooks.
column7:
1. The net subtotal floors at $0.00 (never below).
2. QuickBooks discount lines are CAPPED so they sum exactly to the floored net subtotal — never below it (QuickBooks rejects a negative total, S6-R10d).
3. With multiple discount lines the cap is split proportionally to each line's size, allocated in whole cents by the largest-remainder method: every line is whole-cent, the capped discounts sum exactly, and there is no fractional cent or negative total.
4. The amount removed by the cap equals the carried customer credit (S6-R11).

column1: Verify See Financial Data gates ALL fee/discount dollar amounts everywhere (without SFD, amounts are hidden)
column5:
1. A work order (and a part sale, and a customer) already has adjustments to view.
2. Two ZZAUTOTEST custom roles ready: Role A WITH See Financial Data; Role B WITHOUT See Financial Data (otherwise identical). Use exact-user-match when assigning to Tech (Tech /change staff_id 6fb22c1b-…).
column6:
1. Assign Role A (SFD ON) to the test user; open the WO, Part Sale, Customer F&D tab.
2. Note the fee/discount dollar amounts on: WO sidebar card, WO line table, Stats tab, Financial Info card, Part Sales F&D column & viewer, and customer documents.
3. Assign Role B (SFD OFF) to the test user; revisit the same surfaces.
4. Restore Tech to Time Clock (role 77b069d1-…) when done.
column7:
1. With SFD ON: all fee/discount dollar amounts are visible on every surface.
2. With SFD OFF: all fee/discount dollar amounts are HIDDEN on every surface, and no add/edit/remove control is reachable (S13-N1).
3. See Financial Data is the "pricing-view permission" referenced in Stories 3/4/11.

column1: Verify Whole-WO adjustment add/edit/remove requires Work Orders: Create and Edit
column5:
1. An open work order.
2. Two ZZAUTOTEST roles, both with See Financial Data ON: Role A WITH Work Orders: Create and Edit; Role B WITHOUT it. Assign by exact-user-match to Tech.
column6:
1. With Role A: open the WO toolbar ⋯ → confirm "Add Work Order Fee / Discount" is present; add, edit, and remove a whole-WO adjustment.
2. With Role B: revisit the WO toolbar ⋯ and the WO sidebar card.
3. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. With Work Orders: Create and Edit ON: whole-WO add/edit/remove is allowed and succeeds.
2. With it OFF: the whole-WO add/edit/remove controls are not shown, and the system rejects the action (S13-N2).
3. Editing/removing a whole-WO adjustment uses this same permission (not Delete).

column1: Verify Labor-line and Part-line adjustment add/edit/remove requires Work Order Lines: Create and Edit
column5:
1. An open work order with a labor line and a part.
2. Two ZZAUTOTEST roles, both with See Financial Data ON: Role A WITH Work Order Lines: Create and Edit; Role B WITHOUT it. Assign by exact-user-match to Tech.
column6:
1. With Role A: use a labor line's 3-dot menu → "Add Fee / Discount"; add, edit, remove a Labor Line adjustment. Repeat via a part's menu for a Part Line adjustment.
2. With Role B: revisit the labor-line and part menus.
3. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. With Work Order Lines: Create and Edit ON: labor-line and part-line add/edit/remove are allowed.
2. With it OFF: the line-level starting places (3-dot menus) do not show the option, and the action is rejected (S13-N2).
3. This is the permission the earlier stories called the "Work Order change permission" for line-level actions.

column1: Verify Part-Sale part adjustment add/edit/remove requires Part Sales: Create and Edit
column5:
1. An open part sale with at least one part.
2. Two ZZAUTOTEST roles, both with See Financial Data ON: Role A WITH Part Sales: Create and Edit; Role B WITHOUT it. Assign by exact-user-match to Tech.
column6:
1. With Role A: on the part sale, use a part row's menu → "Add Fee / Discount"; add, edit, remove a Part Line adjustment. Also use the toolbar ⋯ → "Add Parts Sale Fee / Discount" for a whole-parts-sale adjustment.
2. With Role B: revisit the part-sale menus.
3. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. With Part Sales: Create and Edit ON: part-sale add/edit/remove is allowed.
2. With it OFF: the part-sale F&D controls are not shown and the action is rejected (S13-N2).
3. Part-sale adjustments — on the whole sale or on a part line — require Part Sales: Create and Edit plus See Financial Data, and do not use any Work Order permission (S13-R5).

column1: Verify any add/edit/remove of an adjustment also requires See Financial Data to be ON
column5:
1. An open work order.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST role that HAS Work Orders: Create and Edit (and/or Work Order Lines / Part Sales Create and Edit) but has See Financial Data OFF. Assign by exact-user-match to Tech.
column6:
1. Assign the role (change permission ON, SFD OFF).
2. Open the WO and try to reach the Add Fee / Discount controls at every starting place (toolbar ⋯, labor-line ⋮, part menu).
3. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. Even with the change permission ON, add/edit/remove is NOT reachable while See Financial Data is OFF (S13-R6).
2. The controls sit on screens that are hidden when SFD is off, so there is no way to add/edit/remove.
3. Dollar amounts are also hidden.

column1: Verify REMOVING an adjustment is governed by "Create and Edit", NOT the separate "Delete" permission
column5:
1. An open work order with an existing whole-WO adjustment.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST role with See Financial Data ON and Work Orders: Create and Edit ON, but with the Work Orders "Delete" permission OFF. Assign by exact-user-match to Tech.
column6:
1. Assign the role (Create and Edit ON, Delete OFF).
2. Open the WO sidebar card, hover an adjustment's 3-dot menu, and choose Delete/Remove; confirm the removal.
3. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. Removing the adjustment SUCCEEDS on Create and Edit alone — the separate "Delete" permission is NOT required (S13-R7).
2. "Delete" is for whole records (work order, labor line, part), not for adjustments.
3. Removing an adjustment is treated as part of "Create and Edit".

column1: Verify create/edit/delete of an adjustment TEMPLATE requires Settings → Finance
column5: 1. Two ZZAUTOTEST roles: Role A WITH Settings → Finance; Role B WITHOUT it. Assign by exact-user-match to Tech.
column6:
1. With Role A: go to Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts (below Canned Lines); create a template, edit it, delete it.
2. With Role B: attempt to reach the admin Fees & Discounts page.
3. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. With Settings → Finance ON: the admin Fees & Discounts page is reachable and create/edit/delete works.
2. With it OFF: the page/controls are not available (this is Story 7's "administration access").
3. Settings → Finance is the same permission used for tax settings and the QuickBooks connection.

column1: Verify viewing/changing a customer's default fees & discounts requires BOTH Customer Management: Create and Edit AND Manage Accounts Payable and Receivable
column5:
1. A customer exists.
2. Three ZZAUTOTEST roles: (A) both permissions ON; (B) Customer Management ON but Manage AP/AR OFF; (C) Manage AP/AR ON but Customer Management OFF. Assign by exact-user-match to Tech.
column6:
1. With Role A: open the customer page and its "Fees & Discounts" tab; use "Add Fee/Discount" and Remove.
2. With Role B: revisit the customer page "Fees & Discounts" tab.
3. With Role C: revisit the customer page "Fees & Discounts" tab.
4. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. With BOTH permissions ON: the "Fees & Discounts" tab and its Add/Remove controls are available and work.
2. Without Manage Accounts Payable and Receivable: the customer "Fees & Discounts" tab and controls are HIDDEN (S13-N3).
3. Without Customer Management: Create and Edit: the defaults cannot be viewed/changed.
4. This is Story 9's "customer change permission" — both are required.

column1: Verify seeing fee/discount entries in the WO history log requires Work Orders: Create and Edit (line history requires Work Order Lines: Create and Edit) and stays visible even when F&D UI is hidden
column5:
1. A work order already has fee/discount history (add/edit/remove entries).
2. Two ZZAUTOTEST roles: Role A WITH Work Orders: Create and Edit (and, for line history, Work Order Lines: Create and Edit); Role B WITHOUT those. Assign by exact-user-match to Tech.
column6:
1. With Role A: open the WO history log and locate the fee/discount entries; also open an individual labor-line / part-line history.
2. Confirm entries remain visible even when the F&D UI is hidden (Fees & Discounts feature off, or See Financial Data off).
3. With Role B (lacking Work Orders: Create and Edit / Work Order Lines: Create and Edit): open the WO history log and a line history.
4. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. With Work Orders: Create and Edit: the WO history log and its fee/discount entries are visible. Viewing an individual labor-line or part-line history requires Work Order Lines: Create and Edit.
2. Entries stay visible even when the F&D UI is hidden by the Fees & Discounts feature or by See Financial Data (S10-R1).
3. The log shows the SET rate (e.g. "10.00%" or "$5.00"), not a resolved total, so See Financial Data does NOT gate it (S10-R6c).
4. Without Work Orders: Create and Edit the WO history log (including fee/discount entries) is not accessible; without Work Order Lines: Create and Edit the labor-line/part-line history is not accessible.

column1: Verify BOTH gates are required — the Fees & Discounts feature ON AND the matching permission
column5:
1. Ability to toggle the Fees & Discounts feature for the org.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST role with See Financial Data and Work Orders: Create and Edit ON.
3. An open work order.
column6:
1. Flag OFF + permission ON: open the WO and look for any F&D control.
2. Flag ON + permission OFF: assign a role without the change permission and look for the controls.
3. Flag ON + permission ON: confirm the controls appear and work.
4. Restore Tech to Time Clock and leave the flag in its original state.
column7:
1. Flag OFF (regardless of permission): NO F&D controls anywhere (except the history log, Story 10).
2. Flag ON but permission OFF: controls hidden / action rejected.
3. Flag ON AND permission ON: controls appear and the action succeeds.
4. A user needs BOTH the per-org Fees & Discounts feature and the permission (S13-R1).
column8: S13-R1, Fees & Discounts feature + permission (both gates)

column1: Verify add/edit/remove is blocked when the WO is Invoiced/Paid or the user is in history mode
column5:
1. The user has all F&D permissions (so only the WO state should block).
2. An Invoiced or Paid work order, and separately a way to enter history mode.
column6:
1. Open an Invoiced or Paid WO; look for Add Fee / Discount at every starting place and for per-entry Edit/Delete menus.
2. Attempt to add/edit/remove anyway (e.g. via a crafted request).
3. Enter history mode and attempt to add an adjustment.
column7:
1. On an Invoiced or Paid WO: "Add Fee / Discount" is hidden at all starting places and per-entry 3-dot menus are not shown (S1-N1, S3-N3).
2. The system rejects any create/edit/remove on an Invoiced or Paid WO (S3-R1b).
3. In history mode the user cannot add an adjustment (S1 prerequisite).
4. Create/edit/remove is allowed only while the WO is open (S3-R1a).

column1: Verify with the Fees & Discounts feature OFF, all F&D UI and behavior are hidden everywhere
column5:
1. Ability to set the Fees & Discounts feature OFF for the org.
2. The test user has See Financial Data and all Create and Edit permissions.
3. Surfaces to inspect: WO (toolbar ⋯, labor-line ⋮, part menu, sidebar card, Stats tab, Financial Info row), Part Sale (F&D column), Customer (F&D tab), Administration → Service (templates).
column6:
1. Set the Fees & Discounts feature OFF for the org.
2. Visit every surface above and look for any F&D control, card, column, tab, or amount.
3. Restore the flag to its original state after.
column7:
1. With the flag OFF, NO fees-and-discounts controls appear anywhere in the product.
2. No WO sidebar card, no Stats F&D section, no Financial Info F&D row, no Parts F&D column, no customer F&D tab, no admin template page.
3. This holds even for a fully-permissioned user — the flag is the outer gate.

column1: Verify the WO history log STILL shows fee/discount entries even when the Fees & Discounts feature is OFF
column5:
1. A work order already has fee/discount history entries.
2. The user has Work Orders: Create and Edit.
3. Ability to set the Fees & Discounts feature OFF.
column6:
1. Set the Fees & Discounts feature OFF.
2. Open the WO history log and look for the previously-recorded fee/discount entries.
3. Restore the flag after.
column7:
1. Fee/discount history entries REMAIN visible in the WO history log even with the flag off (S10-R1) — the documented exception to "flag off hides everything."
2. All other F&D UI is still hidden.

column1: Verify with the flag ON, the matching permission is still required to use F&D
column5:
1. Two ZZAUTOTEST roles: one with the F&D-relevant permissions, one without.
2. An open work order.
column6:
1. With the flag ON and the user lacking See Financial Data / the change permission, open the WO and look for F&D controls and amounts.
2. Then grant the permissions and revisit.
3. Restore Tech to Time Clock after.
column7:
1. Flag ON alone is not sufficient — without the permission, amounts are hidden and controls are unreachable.
2. Once the permission is granted, the controls appear and the action works.
3. Confirms the flag and permission are two independent, both-required gates.

column1: Verify the Add button stays DISABLED until Name AND Type AND Calculation type AND Amount > 0 are all set
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. An open work order; open the Add Fee / Discount dialog.
column6:
1. With the dialog freshly opened (all fields empty), observe the Add button state.
2. Fill fields one at a time — Name only; then + Type; then + Calculation type; then + Amount = 0; then Amount > 0 — observing the Add button after each.
3. Clear one required field again and observe the button.
column7:
1. The Add button is DISABLED by default and remains disabled until ALL of Name, Type, Calculation type, and Amount > 0 are set (design §6 validateForm).
2. With Amount = 0 the button stays disabled (Amount must be > 0).
3. The confirm button label reads "Add Fee" (Type=Fee) or "Add Discount" (Type=Discount), changing live with Type (S2-R27).
4. Clearing any required field disables the button again.
5. Max Amount / Max cap is NOT required to enable Add.

column1: Verify a blank or 0 Amount/Percent blocks save with an inline error
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. Add dialog open with Name and Type and Calculation type filled.
column6:
1. Leave Amount/Percent blank and attempt to save.
2. Enter Amount/Percent = 0 and attempt to save.
3. Enter a valid value (> 0) and save.
column7:
1. A blank Amount/Percent blocks save with an inline error (S2-N2).
2. A value of 0 is invalid (values must be > 0, §5-R1) — save is blocked / Add stays disabled.
3. A value > 0 (≥ $0.01 flat, ≥ 0.01% percentage) allows save.

column1: Verify an empty Name blocks save with an inline error (Name required, up to 100 characters)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. Add dialog open with Type, Calculation type, and a valid Amount filled.
column6:
1. Leave Name empty and attempt to save.
2. Enter a Name and confirm save is allowed.
3. Try a Name longer than 100 characters.
column7:
1. An empty Name blocks save with an inline error (S2-N1); the Add button stays disabled.
2. Name is required free text up to 100 characters (S2-R19).
3. Input beyond 100 characters is not accepted / is truncated at 100.

column1: Verify a percentage discount > 100% is invalid while a percentage fee has no upper cap
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. Add dialog open.
column6:
1. Type = Discount, Calculation type = percentage, Percent = 100.5 → attempt save.
2. Percent = 100 → attempt save.
3. Type = Fee, percentage, Percent = 500 → attempt save.
column7:
1. Discount at 100.5% is invalid — blocked (§5-R2).
2. Discount at exactly 100% is allowed.
3. Fee at 500% is allowed — percentage fees have no upper limit.
4. Flat Amount adjustments never take a Max Amount (§5-R2/R6).

column1: Verify negative Amount/Percent values are rejected (values must be > 0)
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. Add dialog open with Name, Type, Calculation type set.
column6:
1. Enter Amount = −5 (Flat) and attempt to save.
2. Enter Percent = −10 (percentage) and attempt to save.
column7:
1. Negative values are not accepted — values must be > 0 (§5-R1). The sign (fee + / discount −) comes from Type, not from a negative input.
2. Save is blocked / the field rejects the negative value.

column1: Verify Max cap edge behavior — 0 or empty = no maximum, and Max Amount shows only for percentage methods
column5:
1. Role has See Financial Data and the matching change permission.
2. Add dialog open.
column6:
1. Choose a percentage Calculation type — confirm the Max Amount (Optional) field appears (S2-R24).
2. Leave Max Amount empty and save; then set Max Amount = 0 and save.
3. Switch Calculation type to Flat Amount — confirm the Max Amount field is not shown.
column7:
1. Max Amount (Optional) appears only for percentage methods (S2-R24).
2. Empty Max Amount = no maximum; an entered 0 is also treated as empty (no maximum) in the dialog (§5-R6, S2-R25).
3. For Flat Amount, no Max Amount field is shown (Flat never uses Max Amount).

column1: Verify a template that is BOTH location auto-apply and a customer default yields ONE adjustment on a new WO
column5:
1. A template at the location is marked auto-apply (S7-R5).
2. The SAME template is also set as a default for a customer (S9-R2).
column6:
1. Create a NEW work order for that customer.
2. Inspect the WO's whole-WO adjustments (sidebar card / Financial Info F&D count).
3. Count how many times the shared template's adjustment was added.
column7:
1. The shared template's adjustment appears exactly ONCE on the new work order — the auto-apply and customer-default paths do not stack.
2. No duplicate copy is added (the single add is the settled intended behavior; a double-add would be a defect).
column8: S9 known gap (auto-apply + customer-default duplication); S7-R5, S9-R2
